L3·N10109unmasked layer
This neuron tracks discourse continuity: it fires on tokens that continue an ongoing clause mid-sentence (function words like " sometimes", " to", " is", or the first word-piece of a word inside a sentence, often just after a comma/dash), and is strongly suppressed on capitalized words that start a fresh sentence/paragraph after a newline or period ("This", "The", "Having", "Thank").

L3·N11738unmasked layer
This neuron's strongest (least-suppressed) responses come on ordinary mid-clause function words — the modal "would", determiner "a", pronoun "you", preposition "in" — while it is most strongly suppressed on finite present-tense verbs immediately following a named subject ("Bob offers", "Larry checks", "Lisa is") and on sentence-final periods, so it looks like a syntactic-position signal rather than a semantic detector.
